newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock markets move up after HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China stock markets move up after HK handover.

text.p: China's stock markets moved higher in early trade on Wednesday on the first day of trading following the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule at midnight on Monday, brokers said.
The appearance of a smooth handover boosted sentiment, but large-scale buying was absent as investors had already digested the implications of the event, they said.
But after opening higher, domestic currency A shares in both Shanghai and Shenzhen quickly reversed direction as investors soled and waited for a long term trend to emerge, brokers said.
In early trade, the Shanghai B share index rose 0.065 points or 0.08 percent to 81.543 points.
After a slight gain at the open, Shanghai's A share index fell 10.084 points or 0.77 percent to 1,296.37 points in early trading.
Meanwhile, Shenzhen A shares had fallen 3.02 points or 0.67 percent to 446.41 points in early trading.
"People are pretty excited about the handover, so you got a bit of a bounce at the open," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.

Shanghai's foreign currency B shares and domestic currency A shares edged higher at the open, while Shenzhen's A index rose on selective buying of companies expected to post good 1997 interim results during the July and August reporting season, brokers said.
Shenzhen's foreign currency B shares will resume trading on Thursday.
But Shanghai and Shenzhen A shares quickly moved into negative territory after the opening bell as the Hong Kong handover had already been factored into the market, brokers said.
